findings_to_judge.finding: NSSF-adjusted NICS background checks for the three calendar months that are SPWH's fiscal Q2 (quarter ends 1 Aug 2026) ran May +3.2% (1,105,758), June +11.7% (1,123,006) and July +8.5% (1,061,883) YoY -- roughly +7.7% for the quarter -- versus only +3.5% (Feb) and +1.9% (Mar) in the fiscal Q1 in which SPWH delivered +2.1% same-store sales and +6.3% hunting/shooting; the two strongest months were published on 6 July and 5 August, after management reaffirmed FY comps of -1.0% to +2.0% on 2 June with visibility only through soft May.
findings_to_judge.source_date: 2026-07-06 (publication date stated on page; URL path /2026/07/)

findings_to_judge.finding: The $200 NFA transfer tax on suppressors fell to $0 on 1 January 2026, and NFA background checks have roughly doubled-to-tripled in SPWH's fiscal Q2 window (May 2026 146,551 vs 73,138, +100.4%; June 2026 166,677 vs 60,147, +177.1%; July 2026 130,013, +108.8%) -- and SPWH has been selling suppressors online through a 'Delivered by Silencer Central' drop-ship partnership since 12 March 2025, yet the words suppressor, silencer and NFA do not appear anywhere on its Q1 2026 earnings call.
findings_to_judge.source_date: 2025-03-12 (date in URL path /2025/03/12/ -- deliberately checked, this is a 2025 release and predates the tax change)

findings_to_judge.finding: The 8-K filed 24 June 2026 (event 18 June 2026) pushed BOTH the senior secured revolver (resized $350m to $315m) and the $45m ABL term loan out to 18 June 2031, removing the 27 May 2027 revolver maturity that was still disclosed in the Q1 10-Q alongside $114.6m of borrowing-base availability -- so the balance-sheet mechanism that produced this stock's two extreme prints (-29.8% on 4 Dec 2025, +97.9% on 1 Apr 2025) cannot recur in the same form at this print.

The demand that is accelerating is SPWH's lowest-margin demand: Q1 2026 gross margin fell to 29.6% from 30.4% specifically because firearms and ammunition mix rose while higher-margin categories declined, Q1 adjusted EBITDA was -$8.1m against a full-year guide of $30-36m that is therefore entirely back-half-loaded, and Academy told investors on 10 June 2026 -- eight days after SPWH last spoke -- that it was 'tracking at flat comparable sales through the Memorial Day period' on 'persistent $4+ gas prices'.
findings_to_judge.source_date: 2026-06-02 (Q1 FY2026 press release, thirteen weeks ended 2026-05-02, filed as 8-K Ex-99)

findings_to_judge.finding: NSSF-adjusted NICS for SPWH's exact fiscal Q2 window (May 1,105,758 / June 1,123,006 / July 1,061,883 = 3,290,647 vs 3,055,402 a year earlier, +7.7%) accelerated 5.4 points from the ~+2.3% of its fiscal Q1 (Feb +3.5%, Mar +1.9%, Apr +1.6%), the quarter in which SPWH printed +2.1% comps and +7.4% hunting-and-shooting.

This quarter laps the highest gross margin SPWH has posted in the recent run - 32.0% in Q2 FY2025 - while the Q1 FY2026 it just reported came in at 29.6% (down 80bps YoY) with management attributing the contraction specifically to mix into lower-margin firearms and ammunition, which is precisely the category the NICS acceleration drives.

The 8-K filed 24 June 2026 amended and restated both facilities out to 18 June 2031 - the $45m ABL term loan and a revolver cut from $350m to $315m - so the near-term maturity wall the price appears to embed is gone, and Q1 liquidity was $116.7m against a minimum-availability covenant of the greater of $30m or 10% of the gross borrowing base.
